title: Glaciation
examples: What is the difference between an abrasion and a pluck?
Can you show me a diagram of a U-shaped valley?
How does the rate of melting affect glacial deposits?

explain.say: Today we are learning about landforms created by ice.
Glacial erosion involves the scraping away of rock material.
A corrie is a bowl-shaped hollow carved by ice at the edge of a mountain.
Deposition happens when the ice melts and drops its load of material.
A terminal moraine marks the furthest point a glacier reached.
In everyday life, river erosion and glacial erosion both shape valleys.

faq.q: What is the difference between a till and a moraine?
faq.a: Till is unsorted material dropped by the ice. A moraine is a ridge of till deposited at the edges or end of a glacier.
asks: What is the difference between glacial till and moraine material?

faq.q: Does every valley show signs of glaciation?
faq.a: No, only valleys that have been covered by a significant ice sheet will show these specific landforms. Rivers can also erode valleys.
asks: Can non-glacial valleys look like glacial ones?
What causes the U-shape of a valley?

faq.q: How does abrasion work on rock surfaces?
faq.a: Abrasion happens when rocks embedded in the ice grind against the bedrock, smoothing or scratching it.
asks: What is the process of rock grinding by ice?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a corrie and a cirque?
faq.a: These terms refer to the same feature. A corrie is the general term, and cirque is often used in academic settings.
asks: Are corrie and cirque the same thing?

faq.q: Do glaciers erode both vertically and horizontally?
faq.a: Yes, glaciers erode downwards creating deep troughs. They also erode sideways, widening the valley floor.

facts: Glaciers are massive, slow-moving rivers of ice.
Plucking involves the ice freezing onto and ripping out bedrock pieces.
A U-shaped valley suggests past glacial action.
Moraines are piles of unsorted glacial debris.

quiz.say: A river valley that has been significantly widened and deepened by ice is most likely to have what shape?
quiz.why: Glaciers are powerful enough to carve out wide, trough-like, U-shaped valleys.

wrong.0: Circular shapes are more often associated with impact craters or kettle holes.
wrong.1: While some glacial features are irregular, the main cross-section tends to be consistently U-shaped.
wrong.3: V-shapes are typically formed by the steady downward cutting action of running rivers.

quiz.say: If you find a ridge of unsorted rock debris marking the maximum reach of an ice flow, what feature have you found?
quiz.why: Terminal moraines are specific ridges marking the furthest point the glacier advanced.

wrong.1: Lateral moraines form along the sides of the glacier, not at its furthest point.
wrong.2: Ground moraines are sheets of till left behind underneath the entire ice sheet.
wrong.3: Outwash plains are made of sorted sediment carried away by meltwater, not the debris ridge itself.

quiz.say: Which process involves the ice freezing onto the bedrock and pulling out chunks of rock?
quiz.why: Plucking is the process of quarrying or ripping out large blocks of rock by the freezing ice.

wrong.1: Abrasion is a grinding action, like sandpaper, using embedded stones.
wrong.2: Deposition is the dropping of material when the ice melts, not the removal process.
wrong.3: Weathering is the breakdown of rock by agents like temperature changes, not ice movement.
